children.text: Dr Sanakaradevi’s talks after the bi-weekly pradosham pujas are over at the Nandikeswara temple are always so rich and full of insight. We can rarely sit through them all, but that is no indication of their importance and value to the revitalization of both the Nandikeswara temple practice and to the community as a whole – keep in mind that this temple sits on the edge of what was once the Sankaran kulam, where all the brahmin communities who were associated with the old, un-destroyed Vedapuriswara Koyil once stood. This history is indicated now only by the remnant that is the Shankara Vidyalaya school; all else including the Periya Paarpan and Chinna Paarpan (big and small brahmin) street names are gone, replaced by ostensibly more modern and certainly deracinated ones. Anyway, this evening as we are waiting for prasadam, Dr Sankaradevi recites these lines from Thirumoolar, which reverse the relationship between things–the elephant hides the tree, the elephant is hidden by the tree (in a sculpture). And so on, for Param and this world.
Lovely explanation here by G. Sither
, who is the very Sither sir I met in Thanjavur once, investigating heritage rice cultivation.
The great furious elephant concealed the wood;
Within the wood, the great furious elephant disappeared.
The elements, starting with the earth, concealed the Supreme (Param);
Within the Supreme, the elements, starting with the earth, disappeared.

edits.title: Angalamman Koyil Kali Abhishekam for Theipirai Ashtami
Vedapuriswara Koyil Brahmotsavam Ends with Utsava Shanti and Shankhabhishekam

children.text: Brahmotsavam Day 16, Shankhabhishekam. Went for this at 10:30am. Homam going on, Arjun gurukkal (who was the main priest during the whole Brahmotsavam) leading. Abhishekam was happening, we caught the tail end of it. Homa finished, the 2 kalasa were taken by Arjun and Kalyana Sundara Gurukkals one round about the prakaram, coconut phat near the dhvajastambha, and then the main kalasa into the moola sthanam – Presumably 108 shankha for abhishekam, done one by one unlike Chetty Koyil where it was being done a few at a time – then shift over to Amman sannathi for the second kalasa pour – simple alankaram and deeparadhanai.

edits.title: Varadaraja Perumal Koyil Brahmotsavam Conclusion: Panaka Puja
Vedapuriswara Koyil Brahmotsavam Vidaiyatri: Thirumurai Utsavam

children.text: Brahmotsavam Day 15, Vidaiyatri Day 5. More special than we imagined. Ayyappan swami had said in the morning when I went with Dyuman that today Gurumama would be the Instagram star (ha ha ha). Indeed, it was special. 12 Thirumurai all dressed up to look much like a siva lingam. Naalvar abhishekam in the morning, and they’re propitiated and taken out in procession (ethir sevai), followed by the thirumurai, and finally Chandrasekara and Gauri. Pushpaka vimana alankaram for Siva on Vrushabha. The Naalvar got a chariot, as did the Thirumurai.

Each year a group is called in to sing Thirumurai songs – a mixed bunch this time, not at all all from the Thirumurai. Yennappan allava, from the Nandanar Charitram by Gopalakrishna Bharati. Naada Bindu, which is Thiruppugazh’s last song. Nadaswaram played முத்தைத்தரு பத்தித் திருநகை – which again is Thiruppugazh. “Thodudaiya Seviyan” is a favorite, but I’ve only heard it sung once at the Chandikeswara abhishekam deeparadhanai. The group this time were young girls from Chennai led by a teacher. Each year there’s a different group to sing. I guess it’s a way of encouraging the classical arts and singing in general, which is for its own sake lovely.

edits.title: Varadaraja Perumal Koyil Brahmotsavam Vidaiyatri: Unjal Utsavam

children.text: Brahmotsavam Day 14, Vidaiyatri Day 5. We arrived super late to this, thanks to the delays in the Thirumurai utsavam, expecting to see Perumal in the Vasanta Mandapam swing as it’s been before. But no. He had other plans! When we reached the ardhajama puja was basically concluding. Nadaswarams playing Annamayya’s “Brahmam okate!” Perumal was nicely ensconced in an embellished  kannadi-AC room with lovely Thanjavur paintings on either side, deep within the chamber next to the Kodandarama shrine – fancy! Sitting to the left of his 2 consorts, typical raja style, instead of between them, as usual. I guess after all the work he did, he gets to relax a little! We saw the last aradhanai just before closing.
Perumal’s utsavar already back in the moola sthanam from earlier in the day, Ramanan Bhattacharya said.

edits.title: Vedapuriswara and Varadaraja Perumal Brahmotsavam Vidaiyatri: Chandikeswara Utsavam and a Floral Procession

children.text: Brahmotsavam Day 14 and Brahmotsavam Day 13 respectively, for Sivan and Perumal; Vidaiyatri Day 4 for both. You know things are really closing up when there’s a whole utsavam to Chandikeswara– he’s the last to be offered food before closing the temple at night, the one who follows the processional parades, the great devotee who sits nearby, but outside. And the Perumal Koyil holds grand court as Rajagopalan with a sengkol in his hand, peacock feathers in his hair, and cows at his feet, Sri Devi and Bhu Devi turn into Rukmini and Satyabama. One has a sense of peace, justice and plenty descending on the world.

It’s perhaps fitting that Rajagopal Thathacharya give us some apt closing lines – as he often does, he calls us aside with twinkling eyes and a deeply happy smile because such is the way he takes delight in stories of the Lord, and recites (of course at a moment when the nadaswaram makes it hard to hear anything, even if we are listening with rapt attention) Paasuram 1.1.9 of the Thiruvaymozhi:
உளன் எனில் உளன் அவன் உருவம் இவ் உருவுகள்
உளன் அலன் எனில், அவன் அருவம் இவ் அருவுகள்
உளன் என இலன் என இவை குணம் உடைமையில்
உளன் இரு தகைமையொடு ஒழிவு இலன் பரந்தே.
uḷaṉ eṉil uḷaṉ avaṉ uruvam iv uruvukaḷ
uḷaṉ alaṉ eṉil, avaṉ aruvam iv aruvukaḷ
uḷaṉ eṉa ilaṉ eṉa ivai kuṇam uṭaimaiyil
uḷaṉ iru takaimaiyoṭu oḻivu ilaṉ parantē.
If it is said "He exists," He exists, and all these forms are His forms.
If it is said "He exists not," He is formless, and all these formless things are His formlessness.
Because He possesses both these attributes—of existing and non-existing,
He exists in both natures, spread everywhere without end.
There’s still another Vidaiyatri day ahead, but could there be better lines to end a festival of this sort really?

edits.title: Vedapuriswara and Varadaraja Perumal Brahmotsavam Vidaiyatri: Of swings and pearl carriages

children.text: Brahmotsavam Day 13 and Brahmotsavam Day 12 respectively, for Sivan and Perumal; Vidaiyatri Day 3 for both. Already we have a sense of the festivals coming to a close with these reposed finales. Umamaheswara sits on a swing in the warm night air, a Mutthu Vimanam simpler by far than the one we saw for the Ramar Utsavam some months before carrying Perumal out with his consorts. These are scenes of beauty, the pastimes of the Gods, their slow withdrawal from the peak intensities of the festivals carried out in their own names.

edits.title: Vedapuriswara Koyil Brahmotsavam Vidaiyatri: Thirugnanasambandar Utsavam

children.text: Today is Vaikasi Moola Nakshatram, which marks Thirugnanasambandar’s mukti-day. Thirugnanasambandar’s utsava murti, identifiable by his index finger pointing towards Siva and Parvati in the heavens above, is brought to the Naalvar shrine. They are given a fairly long abhishekam, following which Thirugnanasambandar moves out and straight across to Natarajar Mandapam, where he will be dressed and adorned. With him also moves the modest crowd present. Once ready, he is presented an aradhanai, taken on a purappadu around the prakaram, and then taken straight into the sanctum of his Lord. There’s a woman we see often who is telling me about this – he will receive now the jnana paal, or the milk of wisdom from the Divine Mother. He first faces his Lord, and then diagonally faces the Ambal murti there who gives him the milk of Siva’s wisdom – Siva Jnanam. Lights go off completely for this. The Garba griha is filled with lamplight. It’s one of those unforgettable moments, which is unforgettable because it’s there and gone in a blink.

edits.title: Varadaraja Perumal Koyil Brahmotsavam Vidaiyatri: Theppotsavam

children.text: Perumal is in Kaliyadamana alankaram for Theppotsavam. Here too, as in the Sivan Koyil, the Theppal alankaram is always in an ugra form. The theppal’s circular structure creates a halo, inside which Krishna dances taming the serpent. His right foot planted firmly on the centre of the hood, left foot aloft in dance, left hand grasping Kaliya’s tail and right hand holding the flute – the form is indeed befitting for a scene in the waters.

edits.title: Varadaraja Perumal Koyil Brahmotsavam Vidaiyatri: 108 Kalasa Thirumanjanam and Dwadasa Aradhanam

children.text: The kalasa thirumanjanam happened in the morning for the moolavar. Later there was a dwadasa aradhanam, with the showing of twelve lamps.

The Sapthavarna Puranam recitation was by Ramanan Bhattacharya after the return of the procession. The Sapthavarna Puranam/Sathavaranam Puranam is a traditional devotional text dedicated to Lord Surya, focusing on his 21 names and attributes that remove sins, overcome illness, and bring prosperity.

Saptavaranam, Saptāvaraṇam: Seven square enclosures, one within the other, the innermost containing the central shrine, as at Śrīraṅgam; கோயிலைச் சுற்றி அமைந்த ஏழு பிராகாரங்கள்/ koyilais surri amaintha ezhu piragarangal.
07:00 PM: Chandra Prabhai Procession and Sapthavarna Puranam recitation

Kalasamharamurti alankaram for Theppotsavam. For the Vedapuriswara Koyil the iconography on the theppal is always a samharam or tandavam. Arasoo Swami makes sure we get a ride on the theppal, too! We feel like kids who have been given extra lollipops. We meet the man who has cleaned the kulam. The junior priest acknowledges this and asks him to come for a ride, too, though he demurs.
Another priest speaks to us about two kinds of bhakti – morattuthanamaana bhakti and “silent” bhakti. He observes that the former is growing more prevalent these days.

10:00 AM - Abhishekam – led by Arasoo swami, who kindly allows for a screen to be placed so that the mirrors at the back of the utsava mandapam are blocked and our cameras can feel happier taking photos!

edits.title: A day of Brahmanda Brahmotsavam Events for Vedapuriswara and Perumal

children.text: Varadaraja Perumal Brahmotsavam Day 9. — The ther at the Perumal Koyil is considerably larger than the Sivan Koyil’s. The wheels are of stone and metal, not wood; Vishwaksena draws the chariot, not Brahma. Perumal is hauled up a flight of stairs and placed in the heart of the chariot. A few moments of preparation, a final aradhanai, and the ther sets off rolling. Perumal is grand and magnificent, but the streets struggle to accommodate him. Tree cover amply obstructs Perumal’s giant chariot. Internet cables running across the road wrap around the ther’s kalasa and kodi. The procession is slow and arduous, inching forward in the gaps of laborious clearance. One great tree on Thiyagaraja Street had to be almost entirely felled so Perumal may pass. We almost miss the Nataraja Theerthavari at the Sivan Koyil because of this, but manage to catch its tail end.

The returning half seemed to pass quicker, and it was soon time for the theerthavari in the late afternoon. Perumal’s and his two consorts’ utsava murtis were set on steps that go down to the kulam. In front of them was also the “astra murti” equivalent – who is perhaps Vishwaksena? Perhaps Perumal himself? [TBC]. Upon completing the thirumanjanam, this astra murti was taken down the steps and, with the priest standing ankle deep in water, was given the Sahasradhara Abhishekam. The conch and chakra shaped vessels poured manjal-neer onto the Sahasradhara plate, showering the murti. In the blazing afternoon sun the sight and sound of the cool, refreshing thousand-fold trickles of water were most temptingly soothing to the senses.

The theerthavari is the last of the events that marks the ending of the Brahmotsavam proper. Later today the flag is lowered from the dhvajastambha, declaring the start of the six-day Vidaiyatri – concluding events.

The Sivan Koyil’s kodi comes down sooner than that of the Perumal Koyil. You can get a sense of what the event sounded like, from the songs of the Odhuvars from that their last day of this Brahmotsavam.
7:00 AM - Sri Natarajar Theradi Mithitthal Theerthavari.
06:30 AM - 08:00 AM: Ratharohanam (Chariot Procession) in Mithuna Lagna, followed by Thirumanjanam and Theerthavari
08:00 PM: Dhvajavarohanam (Flag Lowering), Kumbha Prokshanam, Saattrumurai

edits.title: Ghousiga Balasubramaniya Koyil Vaikasi Vishakam Day 4: Pancha Murti Purappadu

children.text: This is a continuation of the utsavam that started with Vishakam, Day 4. The pancha murtis are Vinayaka leading the way, but with Chandikeswara unusually placed next to him rather than bringing up the rear, followed by Murugan with his consorts looking grander than grand (His festival after all), though the consorts are almost hidden by Murugan’s grand swirling garlands, Somaskanda, and finally the Thani Ambal. The pusari we often see in the temple accompanies. Some kids ride along. It is no doubt a grand but somewhat distracted procession. It passes through commercial areas and markets where it seems to meet with reverence and indifference in equal measure.

edits.title: The Thiruther Vizha (or Rathotsavam) on Vaikasi Vishakam

children.text: Brahmotsavam Day 9, the day of the chariot! Is it a coincidence that the Chetty Koyil had its Thiruther vizha on Panguni Utthiram (also special for Murugan) and the Vedapuriswara Koyil has it on Vaikasi Vishakam (Murugan's nakshatra naal)? We arrive as the homam concludes. Even before the deities board the ther, there is magic in the aradhanai that preceded it under the rays of the rising sun. The utsava murtis are kept outside the library-mandapam. We see the completion of the homam; and piercing this sacrificial smoke are the rays of the morning  sun meeting the flames of the aradhanai. The deities proceed to an ul-purappadu after which Somaskandar is raised and seated onto the ther. The ropes are grasped, the wheel-blocks are removed, and after the last of the aradhanais – pull! The ratha of Somaskanda rolls ahead. The ther’s journey around the madaveethi lasts long, and is significantly obstructed by cables and trees, which necessitate immediate chopping and slashing.

Later in the day we do a recording with Thirunavukkarasar Odhuvar. He spoke about the Malaimatri padigam, malai-matri or the malai of words that stays the same when turned around or recited forwards and backwards–effectively a palindrome:
This first line read backwards makes the second line. Discourses can be given on these lines and their poetic construction, but here is a rough translation:
“Are we gods? No. You alone are truly God—yes, indeed!
O great Lord who plays the yaazh, O One of irresistible beauty!
O One who wears serpents openly, O One who made Kama invisible!
O Lord of Kazhi [Sirkazhi], O great Maya! Remove us from the dark impurities of maya.”
This is the third Thirumurai Tevaram song composed by Thirugnanasambandhar. It belongs to the 'Thirumalaimarthu' genre of pictorial poetry for the Sirkazhi Tirutthalam
7:00 AM - 8:30 AM - Rathotsavam (Temple Chariot Festival) or Thiruther vizha

edits.title: Satru Samhara Trishati Homam and Laksharchana in Lawspet
A beautiful backside and an appearance on a horse!

children.text: It is Nammalvar Jayanti, but abhishekam only to mark it since it comes in the middle of the Brahmotsavam.
Vennai Thazhi and Horse Vahana in the evening; Nammalvar Jayanti Abhishekam.

07:00 AM: Vennai Thazhi (Butter Pot) Appearance Procession – with the cutest chaatrified baby backside – Munnilum Pinnazhagiya Perumal (முன்னிலும் பின்னழகிய பெருமாள்), as they say of Namperumal, the processional deity of the Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple.
08:00 PM: Procession on Horse Vahanam–Thirumangai Alvar sits on the horse named Adalma who carried him across various regions as he traveled to visit and sing praises of the 108 Divya Desams.

edits.title: Murugan Abhishekam to mark Vaikasi Vishakam

children.text: The Murugan abhiskekam is a simple but beautiful affair. Not too many in attendance, but it’s done jointly by Gurukkal (for Murugan) and Periyavar (for the Mayil and vel). A family of the ubhayakarars is sitting on the jamakalam outside and watching us. We tell them about the green tint on the Murugan evident only during paal abhishekam – it’s something they did not know. Enchantments are everywhere. We come back later for a small prasadam.
8-9am: Murugan Abhishekam (but always happens a little late)

Bhikshatanar Purappadu was also accompanied by the Kailaya vadyam. We met them near the Mutthumariamman Koyil entrance, which had signs for AgniNakshatram elaneer abhishekam. Another steal-your-heart show. Put me in mind of the descriptions of Bhikshatanar as being so lovely, the women of the town come out full of desire to fill his empty bowl–but their hands and bodies have such heat, the rice they wish to give him turns to ash…
Before the evening’s Purappadu, we sat a while to listen to the Odhuvars sing. We've included the videos here so you can hear along, too. What they sing: Appar (Thirunavukkarasar)

, Pathigam 4.062), Thirualavai (Madurai Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple). I take a photo of their phone where an app displays the lyrics which they are following, though they seem to know this by heart anyway. That is what appears as transcription below:

edits.title: Yellow Churnotsavam and a Blaze of Indra

children.text: We’re a bit late coming to the Churnotsavam, and have missed the turmeric pounding part. This is a ceremony that brings Perumal and Thayar together, so it happens notably after the Thirukalyanam. Turmeric powder (the auspicious among auspicious powders) is prepared and ceremonially offered or exchanged (to celebrate an auspicious union among auspicious unions!). No playful throwing or sprinkling of the turmeric powder happens here, though that may have been a little holi like. Next, there appears to be a Nel Alavu sevai. We think this is a Mudaliar community ubhayam event as we see Raja sir there (who often comes to our aid in making sure we have access and permission to photograph in several temples we see him in, not to mention making sure we get our share of prasadam). Later in the evening, Perumal comes out all dressed in white and enters a golden chariot--my, my does he blaze!
✅08:30 PM: Procession on Indra Vimanam – Thathacharya said: what is different about him tonight? He has no shankha chakra. He is Indra! Narayanaad indro jayate" (नारायणाद् इन्द्रो जायते)

We went to this but caught the Shanmukha Purappadu on their way. The route is down the road next to Ghousiga, then Nehru St., then back on MG road. A bit of a lonely procession. Through market areas with no houses or people coming out with archanai thattu. Pulled by a temple-owned tractor! With some fairly uninterested looking guys. Shanmukha without a thousand mukhas to greet him along the way...

The Ghousiga procession (always with the name "Ghousiga" on the goes past Sundara Vinayaka, and we get pulled into the koyil, run by Rani Ma’m’s family whom we met at the Vastu puja at the Sivan koyil. Cannot help but feel the Murugan brought us here. Cutest place with a little ther of its own to do ul-purappadu. Sapta Matrikas, Hanuman – Natarajar and mini-Naalvar all. She’s the 4th generation in charge of the place. Ladies and their children mostly running the place. Felt like we were called there. Very simple, homey, low-key puja.

edits.title: Thirukalyana Utsavam and the Mappillai comes out on his Golden Elephant

children.text: He’s a groom today afterall, and so the nadai matches that. “Nadai (Srirangam), Kudai (Kanchipuram), Vadai (Tirupati)”, said Thathacharya! My friend Chandra confirmed the place associations, each one keeping its own speciality, and spoke of how her mother would tell her stories of nadai-kudai azhagu or the beauty of these large umbrellas shading the deities on their way. We awoke to such details at this point. I’ll never look again at one of those kudais in the same way again. They’re magnificent, and not merely accessories, but fully protagonists in this street pageant. The men who serve as the Sri Padam are also animators, they choose to walk in a few different ways to bring to life the deity form that they bear. Today is a wild charging elephant, with all the might, force, and energy of a new groom (mappillai), but a purposeful, fast, direct walk is “Raja nadai,” but of course.
07:30 AM: Pallakku - Srinivasan Appearance Procession | 10:00 AM: Thirumanjanam
09:00 PM: Procession on Golden Elephant Vahanam – with elephant nadai on the streets!

edits.title: Elaneer baths as antidotes to Agni Nakshatram

children.text: 1030am is a elaneer abhishekam, aradhanai in the ucchikaalam (after noon) – we went, but did not stay long. This is for the end of Agni Nakshatram, and the abhishekam is for the mula murti. Followed by Alankaram and deeparadhanai. Elaneer is cooling for human bodies, and so is the liquid of choice to cool deities, too, at the end of Agni Nakshatram!
7:00 AM - Silver Palanquin Procession. 10:00 AM - Abhishekam.

edits.title: Of Motherly love and Garuda's grandeur

children.text: The Patrikai lists “Mohini avataram” as today’s alankara, but Thathacharya corrects us. Wrong to call it that, he says, it’s more correctly Nachiyar Thirukolam. He pauses on his way home after the morning’s responsibilities, and pauses to talk to us at the end of the street, across from the (independent) Naalvar mandapam that is at the corner. He speaks about a few things, but this is a key point, so here’s the story:

Kurathalvan was one of Ramanuja’s principal disciples in Srirangam; he and his wife Andal had two sons, Parasara Bhatter and Vedhavyasa Bhatter, both named By Ramanuja himself. Both grew into learned and accomplished devotees.

Parasara Bhatter had profound devotion to both Sri Ranganathar (Namperumal) and Ranganayaki Thayar, but a particular affection for Thayar. He trusted her compassion above all else because he regarded her as the mother of the entire universe—one who never abandons her children, overlooks their faults, and continually pleads for them before the Lord.

Curious about Bhatter’s unusual preference for Thayar, Namperumal one day asked him why he was so much more affectionate toward her. Bhatter explained his devotion, and that he therefore could not regard Namperumal as equal to her in this respect. Displeased, Namperumal challenged Bhatter: he too could equal Thayar in appearance and qualities. The following day, he ordered his attendants to bring Ranganayaki’s garments and ornaments and had himself dressed and adorned in the manner of Thayar. He appeared before Bhatter: now would he be the equal of Ranganayaki?

Namperumal was indeed beautiful, and perfectly adorned. But Bhatter pointed to one thing that could not be imitated: the eyes! Namperumal’s eyes could express both anger and compassion, whereas Ranganayaki’s eyes were filled only with motherly love. The Lord might punish a devotee for his faults, Bhatter explained, but Thayar would overlook them, and intercede with Him, asking that those who had surrendered to her be granted Vaikuntha-prapti.

Thus, in the Sri Vaishnava understanding of the story, Nachiyar Thirukolam celebrates not merely the Lord’s assumption of a female appearance, but the unique compassion and intercessory role of Sri/Ranganayaki. Devotees surrender themselves to her, trusting that the Divine Mother will forgive their shortcomings, accept them as her children, and ultimately lead them to service at the lotus feet of Sri Namperumal.
In the Sri Vaishnava tradition therefore, Nachiyar Thirukolam is the preferred terminology. It really has nothing to do with the seduction of Mohini.

For the evening: Ramanan Bhattacharya had told us: the exit from the temple is what is special about the Garuda Sevai. So be there– was the implication. We obeyed! It was a spectacle, modeled after what is seen in places like Kanchipuram, and we understood from there what it meant to take on the ubhayam of an event like this. Priests were up there with Garuda, fanning Perumal seated grandly in Garudasana. The pictures and videos of the evening speak for themselves.
08:00 PM: Golden Garuda Seva Street Procession

edits.title: One Divine Wedding, Two Guru Pujas, and 63 Nayanmar Utsavam

children.text: The combination today of Guru Peyarchi with Nayanmar Abhishekam and the Thirukalyanam is hectic madness. We decide Arun will stay put at the Sivan temple (where Dakshinamurti is propitiated as Guru as much as the Guru of the Navagrahas is) while I (Deepa) will move to other temples for shorter periods and return. The hope is to catch the essence of everything, but this means timing it all perfectly. And God knows with delays all over, that’s as tricky as it gets. Thank goodness Pondicherry is small though, and the temples are clustered. I catch only a portion of the Nayanmar abhishekam and One of the Othuvars enjoying a rhythmic session with the Thavil player before heading out. I miss the miss the Guru Peyarchi Abhishekam for the Sivan Koyil’s Dakshinamurti
Guru himself, but Arun gets that.

When all the scramble is done, it’s Thirukalyanam today, another ladies’ event! They seem to know when to come, where to sit, what to look for, and what to take away. It’s like a jolly outing! Photos speak for themselves. The event happened in the ardhamandapam, spilling out into the area right of the dhvajastambha.

Saw Ghouse’s son Kadir come pick up some decorations from the Sivan Koyil; he stayed for the Thirukalyanam. Thursday (tomorrow) starts the Vishakam event at the Ghousiga Balasubramaniya Swami temple (Thursday May 27 to Sunday May 30). Friday is the Laksharchanai. Saturday is Murugan’s nakshatra birthday, Sunday is Panchamurti purappadu 7pm

In the evening is the Nayanmar procession, a form of ethir sevai as the Sri Vaishnavas would say, because all face Siva and move backwards in his presence. The procession is led way at front by a group of women presumably from the Nayanmar Sabhai, singing songs. This is quite a stunning procession just because of the numbers, and the uniformity in the variety of Nayanmar forms.
7:00 PM - Silver Rishabha Vahanam (Silver Bull) Procession.
07:00 AM: Pallakku (Palanquin) - Sri Venugopalan Appearance Procession
08:00 PM: Procession on Sesha Vahanam – not sure what alankaram, he’s standing with his two consorts.

edits.title: Guru Peyarchi at two Amman Koyils

children.text: Brahmotsavam Day 4. We saw both processions in the morning and night. Far fewer Kailaya Vathiyam performers today so it’s not as dramatic as yesterday. Pity, looks like we have to wait a whole year for a show like that again!
07:00 AM: Yali Vahanam Procession | 10:00 AM: Thirumanjan
08:00 PM: Procession on Hanumantha Vahanam – Alankaram as Rama, but of course

Missed the morning, but came for the evening, and what a show it was. Sivan’s bhootavahana demanded Kailaya Vadyam. They don’t enter the temple, but wait outside. And when He emerges–they take over. There were lines of drummers and kombu players with their large curved instruments; it was a nothing short of a spectacle, meant to steal your heart away and make you follow this strange man.
The moment recalls the brahmacharin’s questions to Parvati, whose heart is given to Siva in Kalidasa’s Kumarasambhava (Canto 5, verse 66 onwards):
How will this hand of yours, with the wedding thread bound upon it, endure the first grasp of Śambhu’s hand, which is encircled by a serpent? (5.66)
Consider for yourself whether these two can ever be joined: the bride’s silken garment marked with the sign of the kalahaṃsa swan, and the elephant hide that showers drops of blood. (5.67)
Who, even an enemy, would approve of your feet—which used to tread upon flowers strewn in the courtyards—leaving marks of red lac upon the cremation grounds where hair is scattered? (5.68)

Tell me, what could be more incongruous than this: that the dust of funeral ashes, so easily obtained from the chest of the Three-Eyed God, will find a place upon these two breasts of yours, the proper seat for yellow sandalwood paste? (5.69)

And this is another mockery awaiting you: when you, who ought to be carried by a lordly elephant, are seen mounted upon an old bull after your marriage, the common folk will look on with mocking smiles. (5.70)

Two things have now become objects of pity through their desire for union with the wielder of the pināka bow: that radiant digit of the moon, and you, who are the moonlight to the eyes of this world. (5.71)

O fawn-eyed one, is there even a single quality sought in a bridegroom to be found in the Three-Eyed God—he whose body is misshapen, whose birth is unknown, and whose wealth is indicated by his nakedness? (5.72)

Turn your mind away from this unworthy desire. Where is one such as he, and where are you, endowed with auspicious marks? The virtuous do not expect the Vedic consecration of a sacrificial post for a stake in a cremation ground (5.73)
To all of which, Parvati answers:

Though possessing nothing, he is the source of all prosperity; the Lord of the three worlds, he frequents the abodes of the ancestors. He is proclaimed as Śiva despite his terrifying form; for there are none who truly know the reality of the wielder of the Pināka bow.
For my part, I cannot tell whether the Kailaya Vadyam outside the Sivan Koyil that day is the disguised Brahmacarin’s posed challenges or Parvati poised responses. Perhaps, both.

The same day that Vedapuriswara had the Bhuta vahana veethi purappadu, Perumal matched it coming out grandly on a golden Simha Vahana. To match him and accompany him befittingly were saxophone players dressed in yellow with golden instruments, playing a fine street concert (with all the yellow-yellow flowers of the African copper pod tree fallen on the ground where they played). They’d been called in for this. He was indeed gorgeous and grand on his great golden lion–but today Siva next door stole the show.
07:00 AM: Golden Surya Prabhai Procession (Alankaram was Surya-Narayana apparently) | 10:00 AM: Thirumanjanam
08:00 PM: Procession on Golden Simha Vahanam (Arun’s photos, this was the day of the dozen kombu players at the Sivan koyil)
7:00 AM - Sri Chandrasekarar Street Procession in Silver Palanquin.

Up and out by 4am for this! On the surface, I cannot tell too much significant difference between the Vedapuriswara and the Perumal Koyil Brahmotsavams. At the one they sang Ganapati talam, at the other it’s Garuda talam. Perumal veethi purappadu always has a ghosthi behind, reciting vedam. There was no prabandham ghosti in front. On all days Perumal has a thirumanjanam, but utsavar abhishekams (beyond the nitya puja procedures) are not the norm for the Sivan Koyil on all Brahmotsavam days.
We didn’t go for the evening purappadu--but of course he emerged gracefully on a swan...
03:30 AM: Commencement of Dhvajarohanam (Flag Hoisting ceremony)
04:00 AM - 05:30 AM: Dhvajarohanam in Mesha Lagna, followed by Street Procession on Mangala Giri
08:00 PM: Street Procession on Hamsa Vahanam

We reach around 6am. Homam is already underway, kalasas all set up. Some of the Ubhayakaras object to our use of “professional cameras” in the mahamandapam, so we lay off. Rest of the time with no incident. The man from Ellaiamman puja tells us to go upstairs and zoom to take photos. Another who helps carry the vahanas takes me further upstairs for roof level images of the gopuram etc. (he is one of a handful who comes to do the Sripadam work, if that is what it’s called in a Sivan Koyil context, of his own accord).

All the murtis are out and dressed for the event, sitting on tables in the area to the left of the dhvajastambha. The astra murti is on a small stand in front and to the bare left of the dhvajastambha. Eventually this area is cordoned off, so only the priests, players and odhuvars have access.

Once the flag is up, there is a long bali peetham process. At each peetham the priest declares a raagam to be played by the Nadaswaram, and a taalam to be played by the Thavil. These are followed by a few chants seemingly in praise of the deity, and concluded with the odhuvars singing a partial verse. Only then are each of the ashtadigbalis presented rice-balls.

Somaskandar and all the panchamurtis sets out on a veethi purappadu. I have to leave in between as it’s my mother-in-law’s birthday and we’ve to go carry a cake to her. We’ll have to let our photos do the talking until we have time to sit and write full notes about what the Brahmotsavam is and means in Pondicherry. Mornings and evenings are full, and there’s the family and work at home in between. Notes take a back seat.
6:00 AM - 8:15 AM - Dhvajarohanam (Flag Hoisting) and Panchamurti Purappadu

edits.title: Next, Perumal's turn to the Brahmotsavam

children.text: The Brahmotsavam preparatory pujas (Mrtsangrahanam, Ankurarpanam, Vastu Shanti) at the Perumal Koyil start this evening, a day after the Vedapuriswara. The rites happen in the Vasanta mandapam entrance. A small figure, Selvar presumably, is brought out in a pallaq from the main shrine and he stops in the Vasanta Mandapa. Once the pujas there finish, Prasanna is the one deputed to carry the sacralized mud into the yagasala for the Ankurarpanam. The priests take over there once again. The vastu shanti puja is very similar to what we see at the Vedapuriswara Koyil, but without the mandalas, notably absent from Vaikhanasa worship traditions. We’re also not sure of the significance of the little bommais kept around, prior to the mud collection.
06:00 PM: Bhagavad Anugnai, Mrtsangrahanam, Ankurarpanam, Vastu Shanti, etc. (Procession of Selvar Deity)

edits.title: Vedapuriswara Koyil gets ready for its Brahmotsavam

children.text: We happened to be at the Vedapuriswara Koyil this morning, and noticed the ongoing preparations of an all-utsavars-abhishekam. The patrikai did not include this, but we were lucky to be present at the time – or rather exceedingly before time since the delayed ubhayakaras kept everyone waiting, as happens at so many temples all the time. The abhishekam itself though, once it begins, is greatly exciting. The presence of the Somaskandamurti is majestic and vast – one that cannot go un-acknowledged.
At 530pm the Adigu Vinayakar abhishekam was already underway and nearly complete. Arun was unable to come.

The Vinayaka utsavar was brought outside the Vinayaka shrine and dressed up for the evening purappadu. All the other vahanas in dazzling silver were on the other prakaram. A Thiruvasagam group sitting before the Nayanar sannathi continued singing as the Vinayakar puja carried on. It’s Thursday, so Dakshinamurti is also being propitiated nearby. Ayyappan Swami calls me over and gives a mango and a flower from the Murugan sannathi during the sayaraksha naivedyam rounds.

After Vinayaka’s deeparadhanai, the vastu puja begins right in front of the dhvajastambha, conducted by Venkatesa gurukkal who had done the Chetty Brahmotsavam.  He calls two younger sivacharyas over to chant the Brahma suktam, Rudra suktam, and the Vastu gayatri - "Om Vaastunaathaaya Vidmahe, Chaturbhujaaya Dheemah, Tanno Vaastuh Prachodayaat". By the northern entrance, on the floor, is a form of the goddess made in putthu mannu – “anthill-sand”. This is for the Mrtsangrahanam puja. The vastu puja concludes with the burning of the straw vastu effigy, and its dragging for one round around the temple accompanied by thavil on a single, haunting, ominous beat. The man who drags the effigy around is presented with a dhoti before doing so (Arasoo mama calls me over to take a photo), and is only to step back into the temple after bathing.

Vinayaka meanwhile is ready and arrives at the Mrtsangrahanam site, where a puja happens not unlike the one for Thulasi Mariamman at the smeared stone on the footpath. Numerous shanti mantras are heard, a grid is made with kusha grass with rice in each cadre, and milk is poured and flowers are offered on the manvetti. The manvetti is then used to take some of the earth that forms the goddess figure who is dressed in red. Milk is then poured on the “eaten” body, and the collected earth goes into a Kalavai Satti like thing. It is covered with the same red cloth, now bunched and tied so the tied part sits upright like a figure. A malli garland is wrapped around this red upright cloth knot, and the entire basked of earth is placed at Vinayaka’s feet. The purappadu continues until it reaches the utsavar sannathi in South-West corner.

One of the families whose ubhayam this is runs the Sundara Vinayaka temple (built/ begun in 1910). Rani ma’m, together with her husband and a niece from Chennai are the ones sponsoring this event. Once again, it is this network of temple links that leads us on, and Sundara Vinayaka becomes a temple in our list to document.

Mannivannan comes over, introduces me and Arun to the EO, who seems quite friendly and supportive. We also meet other of his friends who seem social media buffs, and Meenakshi who does accounts in the office. She is to introduce me to Gurumama later. Guru mama I also meet but briefly just before the ubhayakara puja in the main shrine, so he’s a little short. Nothing else noteworthy.
Evening preparatory pujas included: Anugnai, Vigneswara Puja and Vastu Shanti

Sri Ellaiamman Puja. We’ve been waiting for this puja, as we’ve been hearing of it ever since the first visit to Ellaiamman–that time when we went in search of one temple, and were led from there, to Mutthumariamman, Kamakshi amman, Ezhai Mariamman and to the big Sivan and Perumal temples in town, all of which are connected to and by Ellaiamman, who was the ellai or border deity for this town. Her temple is marked on early maps–or a “Pagoda” is marked in an area which cannot but reference this shrine.

But the place and presence of this temple in the “network” that is Pondicherry’s ritual life has diminished, and the long Thiruppani or the delayed kumbhabhishekam is not helpful in that–it’s a risky time because such hard-won positions can diminish in prominence or be lost altogether. The Patrikai says 430, but puja doesn’t start till nearly 630 when it’s already getting dark. A man who we will befriend at the Sivan Koyil comes here, and tells us that this puja continues because the family who supported it have bequeathed a property (Rainbow Nagar 3rd cross) or bequeathed the rental income from that property to the temple for this purpose. The elderly lady whose home it was would come herself, but now she is gone and only the money comes. At least that, so the tradition continues. The Perumal Koyil has a similar relationship with Ellaiamman, but they give the money and leave the puja as such (prasadam is delivered to them).

The temple is dark by the time the puja starts. It’s the wooden Balalaya Chithiram image that is propitiated, along with Her bedecked utsavar form. Gurumama comes, along with Ayyappan Swami. Sathis Gurukkal of Ellaiamman is there, the Maniyakarar and the Vedapuriswarar and Perumal Koyils’ EO. All things considered, it’s a simple puja. No Abhishekam as there’s simply no facility for it. Ayyappan swami holds up the screen when it needs to be held up. Deeparadhanai, prasadam viniyogam. Done.
But the large significance of the ordinary in this case is hard to pin down with a single ritual or a few words.

We are hardly known at this temple, so we’re being cautious, but the elder priest (Gurumama) doing the abhishekam doesn’t seem bothered by our presence with cameras at all. There is a small stone inscription near the Durga shrine which tells us who the ubhayakaras are–the family is in attendance, the lady tells me this was her father-in-law’s bequest. The puja follows the usual motions: kalasa, sankalpam, abhishekam, aradhanai, a group of women sit and sing after this for a long time (presumably they come on all Tuesdays for regular rahu kala Durga abhishekams, and today is no exception) while the priest continues to drop flowers at Durga’s feet. Aradhanai after this.
4:30 PM - Sri Durgambal Puja. This is day 1 of the Brahmotsavam preparatory pujas at Vedapuriswara Koyil.

edits.title: Dancers Dance for the Dancing Nandikeswara

children.text: Evening bharatanatyam performance at the Nandikeswara temple. This temple seems to want to make room for all those up and coming and established in the arts to perform. Dewan wanted to introduce us to the man who runs a shop and teaches bharatanaytam (as someone who could help us understand history etc. better) but we had to leave. We end up meeting Vadivelou sir later and seeing him dance at Lalit’s Garden on “Day 0” of the Draupadi Amman temple’s Vizha, some months later. His work and research are on dance forms and motifs. There are amazingly grounded, rooted, well-informed and researched people in all corners of Pondicherry. He runs a footwear shop on MG road close to the temple.

edits.title: The coincidence of amavasya and krittikai

children.text: Today's line-up: Amavasya – Nadu Shanmuga Velayutha Mudaliar samadhi puja. Then: Krittikai – Murugan abhishekam. Both of these are usually held at 5:30pm, but since Amavasya and Krittikai fall together today, samadhi puja was held at 7am.

We went at 7am, Arun battling a cold, and saw Gangai Vinayakar’s opening jala-abhishekam and alankaram. Then walking round the corner, Sivakadhir Swami opened the Nandikeswara temple. After washing some vessels and bathing the Nandi at the dhvajastambha, he headed downstairs to the chamber directly beneath the garbhagriham and performed the amavasya abhishekam for the small lingam on the samadhi. We realised then that the preponing of the abhishekam meant it got combined with the regular jala-abhishekam rather than being a dedicated event. The only speciality for the occasion was the use of paal in the abhishekam, and a coating of Sambal on the little lingam before it got its alankaram. Coming up, he did the jala-abhishekam for the OM stone and the little Vinayaka before the balipeetham. The moola lingam and Ambal also got a jala-abhishekam. Finally there was a deeparadhanai, first at for the samadhi downstairs, then for the moola murtis.
All deities were then offered naivedyam of shuddhannam and ghee.

We hear from him that initially Nandikeswara was the moola murti of this temple, until the Dharmapuram Adheenam advised them that one cannot keep Pashu (in this case Nandi) without the presence of Pati (Siva). The moola lingam and Ambal were then installed.

edits.title: Rainy Friday Abhishekam at a Theruvu Koyil

children.text: Fabulous! There are traditional instruments belonging to the temple, which the players come in to play. They seem just to materialize. They’re then given mariyadai during Maattu pongal. But it’s not just the music, it’s also the priest brothers who seem to move in a distinct harmony with each other, each lamp movement or flower toss done with a certain command, intention, and style. It’s such a pleasure to watch. A lady there tells me that today’s program is shortened because there’s a dance session after, which they just heard about, but otherwise there’s the standard 3 pradakshinas, each accompanied by a different chanting and singing. And dancing!

This music is Kailaya Vathiyam, and these instruments are used only for Pradosham, also perhaps for some other important days. At other times it’s only Nadaswaram and Thavil – with Beri/Murasu only for Vijayadashami. Staying true to its name, the music indeed feels like it is played on the peaks of Mount Kailasa. The instruments used in this Vadhiyam are Udal (the most important, large drums), Thavandai (hourglass-shaped drum carved from a solid block of jackfruit wood or cast in bronze), Sangu or Shankhanadam (Conch), Tharai (a kind of horn), Brahmatalam (large cymbals), Udukkai (the characteristically hollow-sounding drums), Idai vadyam or Thimila (another percussion instrument, almost ghatam sounding, elongated hourglass-shaped), Matthalam (thalatthukku thalaivan! Almost shaped like a mrdangam),  etc. often expanding to 18 musical instruments.
This appears to be the only temple that uses Kailaya vadyam for Pradosham regularly.

We decided at last, to walk into the Nandikeswara temple, which Manivannan Sir from Manimutthumariamman had mentioned a few times. Two younger men are the priests: Sivavijay swami and Sivakadhir swami. Some things we learned:

• This temple is the kula-koyil for Dewan Kandappa/Candappa Moudaliar; it is a samadi koyil for Nadu Shanmuga Velayuda Mudaliar [son of Nadu Sidambara Mudaliar, himself a caste chief, agriculturist and interpreter, belonging to the Tondamandala Vellala community, traditionalist and anti-assimilationist, (1845/1846–1908)]
• All pujas here done in Tamil. Priests were trained by a Tamil Scholar at SRM college, Chennai
• Priest also mentions Dr Sankara Devi who speaks on Pradosham days and other occasions on Saivism at the temple’s invitation.
• Kartthikai Thiruvathirai: Manakkula Vinayakar comes here in golden ther now and during Masi maham
• Siva here is Siddheswarar, Parvati is Siddhewari
• A Youtube video on the temple we found.

edits.title: Ekadasha Rudrabhishekam and Eka Aandu Vizha

children.text: Vedapuriswara Koyil conducts an Ekadasha Rudrabhishekam. The Vedapuriswara Koyil Sirutthonda Nayanar Thirutthonda Sabhai has its Aandu Vizha simultaneously, celebrated in front of the utsava alankara mandapam with recitation of Thiruvasagam all day.

As I (Arun) enter around 915am, I’m met with a sea of Iyers. There is a homam in the middle of the mahamandapam, around the Iyers are gathered, chanting. There must be about 35 to 40 of them. I walk to the back and find the bhaktar sabhai aandu vizha thiruvasagam reading going on. Both the homam chants and the thiruvasagam recitations are heard together over the speakers, but they’re not chaotic – there is harmony to it.
I was delightfully surprised to find the two main priests performing the homam to be Saiva scholars at the IFP, Thirukumaran and one other whose name I don’t recall.

The homam has 21 Kalasas near the altar, which are sprinkled with water and flowers. The homam is complete by 1030am and everybody moves towards the garbhagrha. This is the start of the Ekadasha Rudrabhishekam - dedicated to the eleven forms of Rudra:
Kapali, Pingala, Bheema, Virupaksha, Vilohita, Shastra, Ajapaad, Ahirbudhnya, Shambhu, Chand, and Bhava

The abhishekam procedure is unlike anything I’ve seen elsewhere. The accompanying Iyers fill the ardhamandapam, filling the sanctum with the resonances of their chants. The abhishekam ingredients are poured not directly onto the lingam, but through the jaladhara pot which hangs above, allowing a steady flow down. The entire scene has a deliberate slowness to it which, when paired with the sounds of the many voices, charges the atmosphere with an intense concentration. I only got to sit in the mahamandapam, so I really couldn't tell what was being poured. Once the jaladhara was emptied, water from one of the homam kalasas is poured over, followed by a bucket of steaming water. The curtain is briefly drawn then undrawn to reveal the Deeparadhanai – it is always a magical sight behold. After this the next abhishekam ingredient is poured into the jaladhara, and the procedure goes on. This is done 11 times with 11 homam kalasas, depicting the 11 different Rudras getting assimilated into the Formless One.

Minor notes: The lingam does not appear symmetrical – not sure if it has got misshapen due to slow water erosion, or whether it was already naturally so. Apparently after the 11 abhishekams at the lingam, the rest of the kalasas are offered in abhishekam to Amman. I wasn’t there to see them.
There are 3 events going on, amidst some mutterings and mumblings from the priests
• Chithirai Thiruvonam, Natarajar Abhishekam – along with Naalvar, Pulikaal Muni and Pantanjali. One of 6 annual such events, the most important being Arudra Darshanam

• Thiruvona Deepam or Sravana Deepam – Thiruvonam is Venkateswara’s birth star. There is a small kalasa puja, followed by the lighting of a large ghee lamp and doing one pradakshina around the temple.
• Chithirai Thiruvonam marks the birth star (Thiruvonam/Shravana nakshatra) of Lord Vishnu falling in the first month of the Tamil solar calendar

• Purattasi Thiruvonam is profoundly special for Lord Perumal because it marks the day the Lord manifested on Earth as Lord Venkateswara (Srinivasa) at the Tirumala hills to protect humanity during the Kali Yuga (It’s the last day of the Desikar Utsavam at the big Perumal temple, and day we end up at Thiruvahindrpuram).

edits.title: Marking Theipirai Ashtami with Kalkatta Kali Abhishekam

children.text: An example of how we have had to gather our information, one ritual, festival, day-time-event at a time. Quick visit to Angalamman Koyil to ask about Agni Nakshatram related temple pujas – Sriram Gurukkal mentioned only Agni nivarthi abhishekam with elaneer and placing butter on Amman’s shoulders (? body?), which happens at the end of the 15 day nakshatram period. Agni Nakshatra Dosha Nivarthi refers to the rituals and prayers performed at the end of the 21-25 day Agni Nakshatram (Kathiri Veyil) period to remove inauspiciousness caused by extreme heat and to seek blessings

edits.title: Checking in at Draupadi Amman Koyil

children.text: We missed this but if the Temple’s rocking Instagram page is any indication, it was a spectacle and a half. Enough for us to know not to miss it next year. Khadir Mohammed Sir kindly sent us some videos, which we are sharing here with his permission. Clearly it was a massive Chithira Pournami celebration, so close and yet so far!

edits.title: Slowly, slowly at the Perumal Koyil
